Title: Combined models of membrane fouling: Development and application to microfiltration and ultrafiltration of biological fluids

Abstract: Membrane capacity during the filtration of biotech process streams is typically limited by fouling, which can occur by pore blocking, pore constriction, caking or a combination of the mechanisms. In this study five new fouling models that accounted for the combined effects of the different individual fouling mechanisms were generated. Explicit equations were derived from Darcy's law that related pressure to time during constant flow operation and volume to time during constant pressure operation. The models used two fitted parameters and reduced to the individual models when one mechanism dominated. The applicability of the models to data for the sterile filtration of IgG and the viral filtration of BSA was tested. The combined caking and complete blockage model was the most useful, as it was able to provide good fits of both data sets, and provide good fits of each of the other individual model predictions. The cake-complete model will provide good fits of a broad range of curves where the flux declines in a manner between the extremes of cake filtration and complete blocking. The combined cake-standard and cake-intermediate models also provided good data fits and may be applicable to systems where these models are consistent with the experimentally observed fouling mechanisms.

Laws:
(1) [constitutive] Darcy's law computes filtration flow rate from trans-membrane pressure, available membrane area, resistance, and solution viscosity.
(2) [constitutive] The standard-blocking law gives filtration resistance as a function of permeate volume processed.
(5) [constitutive] The complete-blocking model gives available membrane area as a function of permeate volume.
(14) [constitutive] The normalized flux is determined by the ratio of initial to current resistance and available membrane area.
(18) [constitutive] It computes permeate volume over time for the combined complete- and standard-blocking model.
(24) [constitutive] Darcy’s law relates normalized trans-membrane pressure to filtration resistance and available membrane area at constant flow.
(31) [constitutive] Computes pressure over time for the combined standard and complete blocking model.

Inputs (variables no law computes):
- R_{0}: Initial resistance to filtration
- t: Time.

Model-wide assumptions:
- Complete blocking assumes that particles seal off pore entrances and prevent flow.
- Standard blocking assumes that particles accumulate inside membranes on the walls of straight cylindrical pores.

answer.description: The model describes membrane filtration of biological fluids, with applications to sterile filtration of IgG and viral filtration of BSA. It predicts permeate volume over time at constant pressure or transmembrane pressure over time at constant flow. Darcy’s law is combined with constitutive laws for complete pore blocking and standard blocking, using two fitted parameters.
